question.text: Which party will win the most votes in Spain's November 29, 2026 general election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the party whose candidacies receive the most valid votes nationwide in the November 29, 2026 election to the Congress of Deputies, per the proclaimed results published by the Junta Electoral Central, the Ministry of the Interior or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), after any recounts.

research:
**Spain 29N general election: research brief (as of 2026-11-03)**

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the proclaimed nationwide valid votes for the Congress of Deputies, published by the Junta Electoral Central or the Ministry of the Interior. No results exist yet because the election is on 2026-11-29. Proclamation usually comes a few weeks after election day, which fits the resolution date of around 2026-12-31.
- 2026-11-03: The BOE published the 893 candidate lists after the provincial electoral boards proclaimed them on 2026-11-02. Parties can appeal until 2026-11-05. [cronista](https://www.cronista.com/espana/politica-es/las-juntas-electorales-proclaman-las-candidaturas-del-29n-los-partidos-tendran-hasta-el-5-de-noviembre-para-recurrir/)
- I could not fetch the DatosRTVE polling average page (the tool was blocked). The latest figure I have is the one in the question background: 2026-10-23, PP 31.5%, PSOE 26.8%, Vox 18.7%, FA 6.9%.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The vote is 26 days away. PP leads almost every private poll. The exceptions are the government-run CIS (Spain's state polling agency), The Objective's 27 Oct poll and the PSOE's own internal poll, all of which put PSOE first.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Sondaxe/La Voz de Galicia, fieldwork 26 to 28 Oct, mostly before the train crash: PP 29.2%, PSOE 26.9%, Vox 19.2%. [infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/11/03/el-pp-ganaria-las-elecciones-con-23-puntos-de-ventaja-sobre-el-psoe-y-vox-seria-la-fuerza-que-mas-crece-segun-la-ultima-encuesta-antes-del-accidente-de-trenes-en-toledo/)
- 2026-11-02: Sigma Dos/El Mundo, fieldwork 29 to 30 Oct, after the crash: PP 31.1%, PSOE 24.6%, Vox 19.3%, FA 7.5%. Reporting says the crash hurt PSOE. Sigma Dos's previous poll, published 26 Oct, had PP 30.6% and PSOE 26.1%. [Wikipedia tracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Spanish_general_election), [trthaber](https://www.trthaber.com/haber/dunya/ispanyadaki-tren-kazasi-erken-genel-secim-oncesi-anketlerde-sosyalistlerin-oyunu-dusurdu-961940.html)
- Other polls from the last week of October (Wikipedia tracker):
  - Target Point/El Debate (28 to 30 Oct): PP 31.8, PSOE 25.5, Vox 19.9
  - EM-Analytics (28 to 30 Oct): PP 31.5, PSOE 25.8, Vox 19.2
  - NC Report/La Razón (26 to 29 Oct): PP 33.0, PSOE 25.6, Vox 19.3
  - Hamalgama/Vozpópuli (22 to 28 Oct): PP 32.4, PSOE 26.4, Vox 19.9
  - SocioMétrica/El Español (1 Sep to 1 Nov): PP 32.7, PSOE 26.6, Vox 19.1
  - The Objective (27 Oct): PSOE 29.6, PP 28.1, Vox 20.2
  - PSOE internal poll (25 Oct): PSOE 30, PP 29
  - More in Common (21 to 25 Oct): PP 28.3, PSOE 27.6, Vox 20.8
- 2026-10-28: A train crash at Urda (Toledo) killed 69 people. It was Spain's second deadly train crash of the year. The PP argues it ends Sánchez's chances of a comeback. Vozpópuli says it is too early to measure the effect. [ITV/AP](https://www.itv.com/news/2026-10-29/spain-reckons-with-another-deadly-train-crash-as-election-nears), [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/espana/politica/el-pp-ve-imposible-que-sanchez-pueda-remontar-en-las-encuestas-tras-la-crisis-ferroviaria.html)
- 2026-10-25: Ateneo del Dato/elDiario.es: PP 31.1%, PSOE 27.6%, Vox 19.8%. [eldiario](https://www.eldiario.es/1_cfb02c)
- 2026-10-14: The CIS October barometer had PSOE 34.0%, PP 22.2% and Vox 17.1%. The CIS under Tezanos has historically overstated PSOE. [moncloa.com](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/14/cis-octubre-hunde-pp-psoe-34-3448290/), [Maldita on 2019 CIS misses](https://maldita.es/malditodato/20191111/el-cis-no-acierta-falla-todas-las-estimaciones-de-escanos-de-los-6-principales-partidos-para-estas-elecciones-generales/)
- 2026-10-05: Sánchez called the snap election after Congress voted down two housing decrees.

## 4. Base rates
- PP or PSOE has come first in every general election since 1982 (14 of 14). PP won 6 and PSOE 8.
- The 2023 polling miss is the key comparison. Final private polls had PP ahead by roughly 4 to 7 points. The actual result was PP 33.1% to PSOE 31.7%, a 1.4-point lead, so PSOE outperformed its polls substantially. In 2019 the CIS overstated PSOE.
- Vox has never come first. Its peak was 15.1% in November 2019. It now polls at about 19 to 21%, roughly 5 to 10 points behind PSOE.
- The current private-poll lead for PP is about 2 to 7 points, centred near 5 to 6 points after the crash. That lead is larger than the 2023 polling error, though not by a wide margin.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "Spain General Election Winner" (prices fetched 2026-11-03): PP 86.5%, PSOE 9%, Vox 0.25%, FA 0.05%. I could not confirm whether this market resolves on most votes or most seats. In practice the two almost always point to the same party.
- Kalshi, "Spanish general election winner? (In 2027)": PP 83%, PSOE 12%, Vox 2%, Sumar 3.9%. The "2027" label suggests this is an older market title, so check whether it maps onto 29N.
- Kalshi, PSOE vote share: 64% chance of at least 26%, 43% of at least 27%, 28% of at least 28%, 14% of at least 30%.
- Kalshi, PP seats: median about 135. Vox seats: 60% chance of 65 or more.
- Betting sites also have PP as clear favourite to finish first. [casasdeapuestas](https://www.casasdeapuestas.com/noticias/cis-apuestas-elecciones-generales-29n/)
- I found no Manifold market or expert model giving an explicit probability for "most votes".

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05: Deadline for appeals against the candidate lists.
- Mid-November (date not confirmed): The CIS pre-election macro-survey is expected. Based on its track record, it will likely show PSOE strong.
- Around 2026-11-13 to 11-27: The official campaign runs, probably with televised debates. The publication ban on polls starts five days before the vote, around 2026-11-24.
- Continuing fallout from the Urda crash, including possible ministerial accountability (Transport Minister Puente and Interior Minister Marlaska have been criticised), and housing unrest.
- 2026-11-29: Election day, with the Interior Ministry's provisional count that night. The general count and proclamation by the Junta Electoral Central follow in December. Postal and overseas (CERA) votes can shift margins slightly, but not by enough to change the leader unless the race is within a few tenths of a point.

The actual result was PP 33.1 and PSOE 31.7, a lead of 1.4. That means the polls overstated PP's margin by about 4 to 5 points, which is about the size of the current lead.
- In 2015, 2016 and 2019 the poll leader did come first in votes.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05: Deadline for appeals against candidacies.
- Mid-November: The official campaign starts around 2026-11-13, televised debates are likely, and the CIS will probably publish a pre-electoral survey.
- 2026-11-23 or 24: Spanish law bans publishing polls in the last 5 days before the vote. After that, pollsters publish through foreign outlets (Andorra-hosted sites).
- Political fallout from the Urda crash, such as responsibility and possible resignations at the transport ministry, could keep moving PSOE's numbers.
- 2026-11-29: Election and provisional count. Proclamation comes roughly 2 to 3 weeks later, well before the 2026-12-31 resolution date.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** The election is 26 days away, on 2026-11-29. The provisional count comes that night, and official proclamation follows in December, around the 2026-12-31 resolution date.

**(b) Status quo:** PP finishes first. It leads nearly every private poll by about 2 to 7 points. After the Urda train crash the lead centres near 5 to 6 points (Sigma Dos 31.1 vs 24.6; Target Point 31.8 vs 25.5; NC Report 33.0 vs 25.6).

**(c) Base rates:**
- PP or PSOE has come first in 14 of 14 elections since 1982 (PP 6, PSOE 8).
- No third party has ever topped the national vote.
- Private-poll leaders in the final month usually win. The exception is close races where polling error is large: in 2023 the PP lead shrank from about 4 to 7 points in the polls to 1.4 points in the result.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- **DatosRTVE average, 2026-10-23:** PP 31.5, PSOE 26.8, Vox 18.7.
- **Polls after the crash, 29 to 30 Oct:** these show PSOE falling to about 24.6 to 25.8.
- **Outliers favouring PSOE:**
  - The Objective (27 Oct): PSOE ahead by 1.5.
  - More in Common (21 to 25 Oct): PP ahead by only 0.7.
  - PSOE's internal poll.
  - CIS (14 Oct): PSOE 34 to 22. CIS has historically been biased toward PSOE.
- **Markets:**
  - Polymarket has PP at 86.5% and PSOE at 9%.
  - Kalshi has PP at 83% and PSOE at 12%.
  - Kalshi's PSOE vote-share ladder gives a median around 26.5%, with a 14% chance PSOE reaches 30% or more.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** Fallout from the crash fades. Sánchez polarises the campaign against a PP-Vox government, and left-wing voters consolidate as they did in 2023. A polling error similar to 2023 (about 4 to 5 points) would put PSOE narrowly ahead on votes. A PP collapse that lets Vox finish first is extremely unlikely, since Vox trails PSOE by 5 to 10 points.

**Reasoning:** The base rate and the poll consensus favour PP strongly. The 2023 miss shows a lead of about 5 points is not safe, but the crash seems to have widened PP's margin, and 26 days leaves limited time for a reversal. I anchor on the markets (about 83 to 87% PP). I keep slightly more weight on PSOE than Polymarket does because of the 2023 precedent and the PSOE-favourable outliers.
